name: The Fall of Ameth'Aran
summary: At Ameth'Aran in Darkshore, you search the ruins and read their ancient stone tablets for Sentinel Tysha Moonblade. Their words tell how the Highborne city fell in the Sundering, preserving history largely lost in the War of the Ancients for the Circle of Ancients in Auberdine.

sections.title: Echoes of the Highborne
sections.body: Ameth'Aran was home to Queen Azshara's elite sorcerers, who wielded powerful arcane magic. When the Well of Eternity was destroyed ten thousand years ago, the city fell to broken marble and cracked pillars. The Highborne who died there still haunt the ruins as restless, anguished spirits.

sections.title: Uncovering Lost Chronicles
sections.body:
Few written accounts survived the Great Sundering intact. The War of the Ancients drove night elves into a struggle for survival, and much of their history was lost. Sentinel Tysha Moonblade surveyed Ameth'Aran and found two large engraved tablets, the Lay of Ameth'Aran and the Fall of Ameth'Aran.

Ghostly Highborne specters drove Tysha from the ruins. Their readings can carry the disaster's history to the scholars of the Circle of Ancients in Auberdine.

faq.answer: Ameth'Aran is an ancient night elf ruin in central Darkshore. Ten thousand years ago, it was a city where Queen Azshara's Highborne nobility wielded and studied powerful arcane magic. The Great Sundering brought its fall.

faq.q: Why are there ghosts in Ameth'Aran?
aliases: why are there spirits in ameth aran
faq.answer: Ameth'Aran's ghosts are the spirits of Highborne who lived and died there. The sudden catastrophe shattered the Well of Eternity and fragmented Kalimdor, binding them to the ruins in eternal torment.

aliases: who gives fall of ameth aran
faq.answer: Sentinel Tysha Moonblade is a night elf sentinel stationed along the road in Darkshore. She scouts ancient sites and recovers lost historical records for the Circle of Ancients in Auberdine.

faq.q: Why does the Circle of Ancients want these tablets read?
faq.answer: The Circle of Ancients wants the tablets read because the Well of Eternity's destruction plunged Kalimdor into immense upheaval. Countless libraries and monuments were obliterated, and few written records survived the War of the Ancients. The tablets preserve rare firsthand Highborne accounts of the Sundering.

aliases: where are the ameth aran tablets
faq.answer: The Lay of Ameth'Aran and the Fall of Ameth'Aran are etched into two large standing stone monuments among Ameth'Aran's ruined courtyards. The wandering ghosts of the city's former residents surround them.

faq.q: What happened to the Highborne of Ameth'Aran during the Sundering?
faq.answer: When the Well of Eternity imploded at the climax of the War of the Ancients, massive tremors and arcane backlash tore Kalimdor apart. Ameth'Aran collapsed, burying its citizens and leaving their ghosts in the rubble.

angles.text: As a night elf, you see Ameth'Aran's ruins as a grim reminder of your ancestors' hubris under Queen Azshara. Unchecked arcane sorcery brought catastrophic consequences.
As a mage, you can read the tablets as a glimpse of pre-Sundering elven spellcraft at its height. They also tell of the ruin that followed when that power spiraled out of control.
As an Alliance member, you help the Sentinels preserve Darkshore's history for the night elf leaders guiding the Alliance on Kalimdor.
